question: Does the GPU waste from decode-batch fragmentation remain when the simulator no longer charges a one-request decode batch twice its profile?
intervention: In the run process, ModelLayer.get_inference_statistics subtracts get_decode_inference_time(1) whenever a batch holds exactly one decode request, undoing simulator/event_simulator/model.py:131-132. Simulator source unchanged; unit test in run.py --phase test.
unchanged: Frozen layouts, traces, route price (frozen V3 including its own x2 decode coefficient), gated scheduler experiments/v3_gated_pathspace/scheduler.py, slow-link threshold.

cells.gated: slow-link-gated admission (equals canonical routes on these flat pools)

primary_metric: GPU busy seconds per output token = sum over GPUs of busy fraction / output token throughput (same window)

decision.efficiency_claim_stands: In both C1_single and C2, gated GPU-seconds per output token is at least 20% lower than full-DAG V3 on every one of the three seeds.
decision.partially_artefact: Gated is lower on every seed in both pools but the reduction is below 20% on at least one seed: report the claim as real but smaller without the doubling rule.
decision.artefact: Otherwise: the GPU waste is mainly produced by the doubling rule; the efficiency claim must not be made.
decision.retained_share: Descriptive: (rule-off reduction) / (rule-on reduction) per pool, using rule-on windows experiments/v3_cycle_pricing/runs/formal/C1_single/v3_seed*.json, experiments/v3_gated_pathspace/runs/formal/C1_single/gated_seed*.json and experiments/v3_gated_generalization/runs/formal/C2/*_seed*.json.
decision.reported_not_decisive: Mean decode batch, one-request batch share, throughput, P95 TTFT/TPOT, completion, backlog.
decision.failures: Failed windows are kept as .failure.json and count as not supporting the claim; no reruns to fill the table.
